newsitem.title: GERMANY: N.Europe rapeseed looks set to ease in June/July.
newsitem.headline: N.Europe rapeseed looks set to ease in June/July.

text.p: Rapeseed prices in Northern Europe look set to drift lower as good North American soybean weather pressurises the Chicago soybean complex, brokers said on Friday.
They also cited a lack of buyers, nearly ideal crop weather in Germany with plenty of rain, and rapeseed area expansion in Germany, Britain and France.
The rain should offset potentially damaging effects from earlier moisture deficits.
"New crop markets have been very slow for a month now, and sellers are likely to store the new crop away rather than sell it at unattractive prices," one broker said.
But some price support in the old crop market was expected to arise from gaps in processors' July cover.
Old crop rapeseed free Hamburg last traded at 485 marks a tonne cif, having held mostly steady in June.
New crop buyers were also little changed from end-May levels at 452 marks, with sellers at 460 basis August/October.
The ex-harvest price range was 447/455 marks.
Rapeseed prices for delivery at points other than Hamburg were in a 437-452 marks range for July (old crop) while August prices ranged between 435 and 452.50, depending on delivery point and terms.
Brokers said rapemeal demand was muted while oil business was more active.
November rapeseed on the Matif futures exchange last traded at 455 marks, up one from the previous close.
Spot meal was at 29.50 marks/100 kg, down one mark from end-May, first half July was unchanged at 29.50 and August-October at 25.00 (25.25).
Rape oil prices had eased slightly, with July sellers at 93.75 marks, and August/October at 92.25.
